rationale: PY-12. `exports` is a relationship type the analyzer EMITS and that no python fixture pinned, while `requiredKinds` did not list it either — so nothing in the repository could see it. Two gates missing is how a relation survives a full review cycle: the fixture lane has nothing to assert and the completeness gate has nothing to require. `overrides` had the same hole (emitted 428 times over 150 ansible files, absent from requiredKinds) and it is the relation PY-6, PY-7 and PY-8 all concern. Adding both to requiredKinds turned section B red on `exports` alone, and this fixture is what closed it. `__all__` is pinned because it is the only export declaration python has: a module's public surface is stated in one list, read by every packaging tool and linter, and an analyzer that ignores it reports a surface the author explicitly contradicted. Six properties, four derived and two declared as BOUNDARIES with forbid rows so that closing a boundary later fails this fixture deliberately rather than silently. (1) A TUPLE is the same declaration as a list — measured over 400 pinned corpus files, 3 of 16 `__all__` assignments were tuples and produced no edge at all, so 19% of the declared surface was invisible for a reason that had nothing to do with the author. (2) A LEADING UNDERSCORE IS NOT A FILTER: `_private_function` is exported because the AUTHOR put it in `__all__`. A rule filtering on the underscore would drop it, and would agree with a correct lane only by accident. (3) A NAME inside the literal is not read: `_EXPORTED_BY_TUPLE` is a variable, and reading it is a data-flow question, not a read. (4) The SET is the claim, not the order — nothing here may depend on position. (5) DECLARED: an `__all__` built by CONCATENATION is not read, and nor is `__all__.extend(...)`. Both are forbid rows: a missing edge rather than a wrong one, and pinning the absence means implementing either one later has to update this file on purpose. A second harness invariant also applied here and is worth naming: the fixture runner refuses a module that exports the SAME name twice, so the two `__all__` assignments above carry disjoint names. That is a real constraint of the export surface rather than a harness quirk — `from mod import *` binds each name once — and it is why this fixture cannot demonstrate 'a later `__all__` overwrites an earlier one' by reusing a name. It demonstrates the opposite and more useful thing: BOTH assignments are read, so a module that builds its surface in two places publishes both halves.

expectRelationships.note: TUPLE spelling — read as of PY-14
the SECOND `__all__` is read too — a later assignment does not shadow an earlier one

forbidRelationships.note: DECLARED BOUNDARY: a NAME in the literal is not read. It is a variable reference, and resolving it is a data-flow question rather than a syntactic read
DECLARED BOUNDARY: `__all__.extend([...])` is a method call on the list, not an assignment
DECLARED BOUNDARY: a concatenated `__all__` is a binary expression, not a list or tuple literal

expectSymbolCount.name: _private_function
expectSymbolCount.note: declared, and EXPORTED because the author put it in `__all__` — the underscore is not a filter

expectSymbolCount.name: _EXPORTED_BY_TUPLE
expectSymbolCount.note: a module-level assignment IS a declaration; the container is a symbol even though the string inside it is only an export

forbidSymbols.name: a_name_in_dunder_all_that_this_module_never_defines
forbidSymbols.note: an `__all__` entry is an export EDGE, not a declaration — publishing one as a symbol would invent a definition that does not exist

_seamNote.what: Exports are derived SYNTACTICALLY: a `list` or `tuple` LITERAL assigned directly to `__all__`. Every `__all__` assignment in a file is read, so a later one does not shadow an earlier one — which is why `PublicClass` appears twice above.
_seamNote.why: The syntactic scope is chosen so the relation cannot fabricate: resolving `_A + _B`, a name, or `.extend()` requires evaluating an expression, and an analyzer that guesses at a module's public surface from a partial read reports a surface the author did not state. The two boundaries are pinned with forbid rows rather than left as prose, so implementing either later has to update this fixture deliberately — a boundary nobody can fail is a boundary nobody will notice crossing. Every edge carries the STRING's own line rather than the assignment's, so a reader is sent to the name they are importing rather than to the list it sits in, and `evidenceClass: structural` because the link between a module and a name it declares is read from the module's own AST rather than inferred.
